title: Compatibility shim risk register and canonicalization heuristics for OpenAI Responses parity
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Short overview: produce a concise risk register and set of canonicalization heuristics for the OpenAI Responses compatibility shim. Goal: enumerate behavioral deltas, rank by customer impact and implement mitigations we can ship as incremental runtime fallbacks and test canaries.
background: We have multiple open tickets cataloging mapping deltas between Redwood Responses and OpenAI Responses. Field reports show customer applications failing due to subtle differences in streaming events, function-calling signals and structured output wrappers. We need a concise artifact that prioritizes mitigations, clarifies which deltas must be fixed vs accepted, and defines canary plans for runtime shims.
scope: In-scope: runtime shim behaviors, event canonicalization, deterministic tool-calling signals, streaming boundary handling, structured output label normalization, canary matrix across model families. Out-of-scope: long-term changes to canonical API surface, licence-level transformations, model weight changes.
acceptance_criteria: Risk register enumerates >=15 distinct parity gaps with severity and suggested mitigations
Each high/medium risk has an owner and a proposed canary plan
Shim implementation proposals include performance impact estimates (p50/p95 tokens)
Canary test harness added to responses-interop CI with at least 5 representative prompts
Documentation draft for engineering + support created and linked

risks: Behavioral drift: canonicalization may hide model-specific signals that downstream clients rely on
Performance regression: additional event mapping and wrapper logic increases per-token overhead
False positives in tool-calling: heuristics could misclassify user text as tool calls
Customer confusion: naming differences may lead to mismatched expectations during rollout
Incomplete coverage: edge cases for streaming interruptions and partial function arguments
mitigations: Add a lightweight opt-in header X-Responses-Compat=shim to allow bailouts for customers
Run perf-sensitive sections in native runtime kernels and minimize JSON transformations
Introduce a confidence score threshold for tool-call detection and surface it in debug logs
Publish a compatibility matrix and examples in the docs; include migration checklist
Expand canary suite to include simulated network interruptions and partial KV cache states
test_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer covering 100+ event permutations
Integration canaries across 3 model families (tiny, base, large) and 2 latency regions
Automated fuzzing to surface tool-calling false positives with synthetic prompts
Load test measuring p50/p95 token latency with and without shim under target throughput
Post-canary monitoring: user-level regression alerts tied to prompt evaluation set
